newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks have no request on Thai rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks have no request on Thai rescue plan.

text.p: Japan's major banks have not been asked by the government of Thailand to participate in a multi-billion dollar financial rescue plan to shore up its reserves and ease a credit crunch, bankers said on Thursday.
They added, however, that at least some Japanese banks are likely to participate in a rescue scheme if they are asked to do so.

"This is because Japanese banks and corporations have already made a substantial commitment to the Thai economy through their direct investments, such as setting up branches and production centres there," said a senior Japanese banker who declined to be identified.
Officials at Sakura Bank Ltd and Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd said they had not received any requests for assistance from either the Thai government or Japan's Finance Ministry.

Thailand plans to raise a total of $10 billion, consisting of $5 billion in loans from banks and $5 billion in bond issues, in order to replenish reserves that were severely depleted when it defended its currency against speculative attacks in May.

"Since the details of the overall scheme have not been unveiled and it is uncertain how much of the burden will be shouldered by the public and private sectors, we can't give any details," said one Japanese bank official who declined to be named.
He said a senior official from Japan's Ministry of Finance has been in Thailand to negotiate the overall scheme.
Japanese banking sources said Thailand's Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya will explain to Japanese bankers the recent situation surrounding the Thai currency during his visit here next week.

Thanong and Thai Foreign Affairs Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn will meet representatives from Japanese commercial banks on July 17, the sources said. The two ministers will be in Tokyo on July 17 and 18 for an unofficial visit.
Separately, a Thai embassy official in Tokyo said Thanong is scheduled to meet Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita and Sakura Bank officials during his visit.

Sakura and Tokyo-Mitsubishi, which were allowed several years ago to open branches in Thailand and offer full banking services there, are expected to play a key role in arranging any loans or other financial help for Thailand from private Japanese banks.
Officials from other major Japanese banks also said they had not received any requests regarding the rescue plan.
An official at a major Japanese long-term credit bank said neither its Thai branches nor its Tokyo headquarters had received any formal request from the Thai government to participate in the plan.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily said on Thursday that Japan's government and financial sector would take a leadership role in extending financial aid to Thailand, working alongside international organisations and other countries.

Japanese Finance Ministry officials said that no requests had been made from Thailand and that the ministry could not comment on the Thai loan package, although they said the ministry will keep in close contact with Thai authorities.
